subsystems.name: Observation layer
subsystems.role: gathers the digital traces of work without interrupting it.
parts: endpoint agents (window focus, app switches, screen frames)
SaaS API and webhook taps (tickets, chats, documents, code)
central event bus with timestamps and user IDs

subsystems.name: Identity and permission mapping
subsystems.role: makes sure a reconstructed page is only visible to people who could see the source material.

subsystems.name: Workflow reconstruction
subsystems.role: turns a messy event stream into repeatable procedures.
parts: variant clustering across people and teams

subsystems.name: Knowledge synthesis
subsystems.role: writes and updates the wiki text itself.
parts: retrieval-augmented generation over a vector index and knowledge graph
citation linker back to source events

subsystems.name: Governance and privacy
subsystems.role: keeps observation lawful, bounded and auditable.

subsystems.name: Curation interface
subsystems.role: puts a human between machine drafts and the published page.

buildSteps.title: Connect the sources
buildSteps.detail: Wire the enterprise directory, chat, ticketing, document and version-control systems into a single event stream, plus an endpoint agent for activity that never reaches a server.

buildSteps.title: Set consent, scope and redaction
buildSteps.detail: Each team opts in per tool and per data type; rules strip personal data, credentials and anything outside the agreed scope before storage.

buildSteps.title: Capture low-level events
buildSteps.detail: Record app focus changes, document and ticket IDs, command invocations and clipped screen regions, all time-stamped. Content is captured only where consent allows.

buildSteps.title: Sessionise and correlate
buildSteps.detail: Group events into work sessions, then apply process-mining techniques to recover the order of steps and the tools involved.

buildSteps.title: Find stable procedures
buildSteps.detail: Keep sequences that recur across people and weeks; discard one-off or low-confidence paths. Score each candidate with a confidence value.

buildSteps.title: Draft articles
buildSteps.detail: A long-context model writes a step-by-step page from the winning sequence, grounding every claim in retrieved source events and emitting links to them.

buildSteps.title: Diff against the live wiki
buildSteps.detail: Compare the draft with existing pages to detect stale steps, contradictions and gaps; propose edits rather than blind overwrites.

buildSteps.title: Review, publish, version
buildSteps.detail: A domain expert edits and approves; the change is committed with authorship, provenance and a rollback path.

buildSteps.title: Watch for drift
buildSteps.detail: Monitor the event stream for divergence from the published procedure and regenerate drafts, lowering confidence where evidence thins.

prerequisites.why: summarising hours of interleaved events into readable steps needs very large context windows.
keeps generated text anchored to real source records instead of plausible invention.
supplies the statistical backbone for inferring ordered workflows from raw logs.
a wiki page built from several systems must inherit the strictest source permission, which few pipelines enforce today.
detecting personal data before it leaves the endpoint is the difference between a useful tool and a compliance breach.

pathway.milestone: assistants that draft pages from tickets, meeting notes and repositories
pathway.unlocks: faster onboarding and less manual documentation.

pathway.milestone: per-team workflow capture with human review before every publish
pathway.unlocks: runbooks that track the real process rather than the intended one.

pathway.milestone: cross-tool process graphs with inherited permissions and provenance
pathway.unlocks: living documentation that doubles as audit evidence.

pathway.milestone: knowledge bases that flag process friction, not just describe it
pathway.unlocks: feedback from the record of work into how work is designed.
